questions.question: On roadways, bicycles are considered:

options.text: Hazards.
Vehicles.
Dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicles.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are vehicles on roadways. Bicyclists and drivers must follow the same traffic rules.

questions.question: Oncoming vehicles are on your left. Parked vehicles are on your right. You should steer:

options.text: Closer to the oncoming vehicles than the parked vehicles.
Closer to the parked vehicles than the oncoming vehicles.
In the middle between the oncoming and parked vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the middle between the oncoming and parked vehicles.
questions.explanation: Steer a middle course between the oncoming cars and the parked cars. This splits the difference and keeps you safe from both.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light means:

options.text: The same thing as a yield sign.
The light is about to turn green.
The same thing as a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same thing as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop completely. Yield to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when it is safe. This is the same as a stop sign.

questions.question: The road ahead is covered by heavy smoke. You should:

options.text: Turn on your four-way flashers and continue.
Slow down, move to the right, and stop off the roadway.
Turn on your high beam headlights and continue.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to the right, and stop off the roadway.
questions.explanation: Slow down right away. Drive as far right as possible and stop off the road. Then decide if it is safe to continue. Heavy smoke can damage your eyes and lungs.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrian crossing.
Side road.
Railroad ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign shows a pedestrian crosswalk ahead.

questions.question: Large trucks lose speed when:

options.text: Driving up long or steep hills.
Driving in long, gradual curves.
Driving down long, gradual hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving up long or steep hills.
questions.explanation: Large trucks take longer to speed up than smaller vehicles. They lose speed going uphill. Give trucks extra space, especially on hills.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is a steep hill ahead.
No trucks are allowed on the upcoming hill.
A logging road is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns about a steep hill ahead. Slow down and control your speed to protect your brakes.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Not assume the other driver will make space for you to return to your lane.
Assume the other driver will let you pass if you use your turn signal.
Assume the other driver will maintain a constant speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not assume the other driver will make space for you to return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Even with a turn signal, do not assume other drivers will give you space. They may not move or let you pass.

questions.question: In fog or mist, never use high beam headlights because:

options.text: The light will reflect back into your eyes.
Approaching vehicles might not see you.
Vehicles behind you may follow too closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light will reflect back into your eyes.
questions.explanation: In fog or mist, high beams reflect back into your eyes. Use low beams instead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks entering.
Truck exit only.
Steep downgrade ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep downgrade ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road slopes down steeply ahead. Check your brakes.

questions.question: A car is following you too closely on a two-lane road. You should:

options.text: Slowly reduce your speed to let the tailgater pass you.
Speed up to increase the distance between you and the other car.
Apply your brakes to slow down, then resume your original speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly reduce your speed to let the tailgater pass you.
questions.explanation: If no lane is available to merge into, slowly reduce your speed. This encourages the tailgater to drive around you.

questions.question: Yellow lines separate:

options.text: Traffic lanes on one-way streets.
Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
All carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mark the center of two-way roads. A solid yellow line means do not cross. A broken yellow line means you can cross to pass if it is safe.

questions.question: When passing, return to your original lane when:

options.text: You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
You have cleared the front bumper of the passed vehicle.
You are 50 feet in front of the passed vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Return to your lane only when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your mirror. This means you have enough room to safely pull in front.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You can travel in either direction in this lane.
There is two-way traffic.
You are approaching a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is two-way traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that traffic moves in both directions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Come to a complete stop as quickly as possible.
Stop and proceed only when the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and be careful. You do not have to stop completely.

questions.question: As you approach the top of a hill, you should:

options.text: Speed up slightly.
Be ready to stop if needed.
Keep the same speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: You cannot see what is on the other side of a hill or around a curve. A vehicle could be stopped out of sight. Slow down as you approach hills and curves so you can stop safely if needed.

questions.question: You should not use your horn:

options.text: When you cannot see ahead clearly.
If you might hit another vehicle.
Near blind pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near blind pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Using your horn near a blind pedestrian can be dangerous. Yield to the pedestrian and go when it is safe.

questions.question: Alcohol in any amount is:

options.text: A stimulant.
A depressant.
Neither of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows down your nerve impulses and body functions. It reduces your ability to concentrate and stay alert.

questions.question: Having a driver license is a:

options.text: Requirement.
Privilege.
Right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Privilege.
questions.explanation: Driving is a privilege, not a right. All drivers must keep everyone safe on the road. If you misuse this privilege, it can be taken away.

questions.question: Your wheels have left the pavement. What should you do first?

options.text: Turn the steering wheel slightly left to get back on the road.
Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and brake gently.
Brake hard and turn the steering wheel sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and brake gently.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly. Release the gas pedal and brake gently. Wait until you slow down, check traffic, and find a safe place to return to the road. Do not jerk the wheel suddenly, as this can cause you to lose control or drift into other lanes.

questions.question: You want to turn left at an upcoming corner. You must yield to:

options.text: Oncoming vehicles that are also turning left.
All vehicles coming toward you.
Pedestrians on the sidewalk waiting for a walk signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: All vehicles coming toward you.
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to pedestrians, bicycles, and all vehicles with a green light coming toward you.

questions.question: When a school bus has red lights flashing, you must stay stopped until:

options.text: All students are off the bus.
The stop arm is pulled in.
The stop arm is pulled in and the bus starts moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: The stop arm is pulled in and the bus starts moving.
questions.explanation: Stay stopped until the red lights are off, the stop arm is pulled in, and the bus begins moving again.

questions.question: When turning left from a two-way street to a one-way street, turn into:

options.text: Any lane.
The first lane.
The second lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The first lane.
questions.explanation: Always turn into the first available legal lane in the direction you are turning.

questions.question: A broken yellow centerline means:

options.text: You cannot pass.
You can pass on the right when the way is clear.
You can pass on the left when the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass on the left when the way is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow centerline allows passing on the left when no traffic is coming. Never cross a solid yellow line to pass.

questions.question: You hit a parked car and cannot find the owner. What must you do?

options.text: Call your insurance company when you get home.
Wait for the owner to return.
Leave a note with your name and address on the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a note with your name and address on the car.
questions.explanation: Leave a note with your name, phone number, and address on the vehicle you hit.

questions.question: In a moving vehicle on a highway, it is:

options.text: Illegal to drink alcohol or have open alcohol containers.
Legal to drink alcohol if you are not driving.
Legal to drink alcohol if you are not drunk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Illegal to drink alcohol or have open alcohol containers.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive under the influence. Neither drivers nor passengers can drink alcohol or have open alcohol containers in a moving vehicle.

questions.question: At an intersection where you cannot see clearly to the side, you should:

options.text: Slow down and look both ways.
Keep your speed and look both ways.
Stop, then move forward slowly until you can see both directions clearly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then move forward slowly until you can see both directions clearly.
questions.explanation: Slow down when approaching an intersection. If you cannot see clearly, stop completely. Move forward slowly until you can see clearly in all directions.

questions.question: Alcohol is:

options.text: A stimulant.
An antihistamine.
A depressant.

questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It dulls your judgment and makes your reflexes slow and unreliable.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while driving:

options.text: Brake lightly.
Pump the brakes.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake lightly.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel tightly and keep the vehicle straight. Slow down gradually by releasing the gas pedal and braking gently.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No passing zone.
Slow-moving vehicle.
Two-way traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone.
questions.explanation: A yellow triangle sign with black words means no passing zone. It is placed on the left side of roads where you cannot pass other vehicles.
